query: Caught in the Reeds Further along the shore a first-year is crying quietly. Their lantern caught in the reeds a few yards out, and it is guttering, wish and all. Wade in and free it The water is shockingly cold. You lift the lantern clear and push it out, and it catches the air and goes. The first-year looks at you as if you'd done magic, which, in a way, you have. Tell them wishes don't need lanterns You sit with them on the bank and say the true thing: the wish counts when you make it. They stop crying. The lantern goes out in the reeds, and neither of you watches.
